## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Paṇṇikajātaka* (Ja 102), translated as *The Greengrocer*, is a birth-story preserved in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. The frame story takes place at Jetavana, where the Buddha recounts the narrative regarding a lay disciple from Sāvatthī who earned his living as a greengrocer selling diverse roots, vegetables, and pumpkins [SuttaCentral]. The greengrocer had a daughter who was both virtuous and pretty, but who laughed constantly; when a marriage proposal was made by a family of equal standing, the father resolved to test her chastity beforehand to ensure she would not bring disgrace upon her parents [SuttaCentral].
Having tested her and heard her declare that she had successfully preserved her virtue, the father escorted her home, celebrated the wedding, and sent her to her new family [Fausböll 1877]. Following this account, the Buddha expounds the Four Noble Truths, leading the lay greengrocer to attain the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphala*) [Fausböll 1877]. In the birth-story's identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha explains that the father and daughter were the same individuals in both lifetimes, whereas he himself was the tree deity (*rukkhadevatā*) who had observed the test directly [Fausböll 1877].
No curated parallels in other languages are recorded on SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus identifies no Pali-internal text reuse or cross-language matches scoring 10 or higher [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records four translations of the story across four languages [SuttaCentral].
